events.text: A tea seller closes the shutters while you are still in the shop. {He} sets out two cups and says nothing for the time it takes the water to cool. "You came in angry," {he} says finally. "You will go out angry. But I can show you where to put it."

choices.text: Stay, and learn to pour

effects.log: {npc} corrects your wrist nine times. By the tenth pour you have forgotten what you came in for. (The Way of Tea begun.)

choices.text: Thank {him} for the cup and go

effects.log: Good leaf. {npc} nods as if that was also an answer.

events.text: An old clerk watches you count change on a bridge and laughs out loud. "Three mistakes, and all three in the seller's favour." {He} takes an abacus out of {his} sleeve as another person might take out a knife. "Sit. It is the only weapon that gets stronger when you are asleep."

choices.text: Learn the clerk's way

effects.log: By nightfall you have found the three mistakes, and two more nobody mentioned. (Merchant's Reckoning begun.)

choices.text: Tell {him} silver is not your road

effects.log: "It is everybody's road," {npc} says, and goes back to the bridge to wait for the next one.

events.text: A trapper with one ear is skinning something by the road, and tells you without looking up that you walked past a sleeping bear a mile back. "It let you. Do you know why?" {He} points the knife at the track at your feet, which you had not seen. "Sit down, then."

choices.text: Sit down and learn to read it

effects.log: {npc} walks you through a winter of spoor in one afternoon, and gives you a vial for your trouble. (Beast Lore begun.)

choices.text: Thank {him} and take the long way round

effects.log: You take the long way round. You sleep very well.

events.text: An old herb-wife pulls a weed out of your hand before you have finished picking it. "That one kills goats," {he} says. {He} looks at the whole slope, once, the way a magistrate looks at a witness. "Everything you want grows on the north side. Nobody told you. Come."

choices.text: Follow {him} up the slope

effects.log: You come down with a basket, and a slope you will never see the same way again. (Field-Reading begun.)

choices.text: Keep your own basket

effects.log: You keep picking where you were picking. You leave out the one that kills goats.

events.text: A monk at a roadside shrine has not moved since you passed it this morning. On your way back at dusk you see the moss on {his} sleeve, and then {his} eyes open. "Your breath leaks," {he} says, as if mentioning a roof. "Each failed gate, you throw away a year. Why do you do that?"

choices.text: Ask {him} how not to

effects.log: One breath a day for a month, then fewer. You had not known how much of you was hurrying. (Turtle Breath begun.)

choices.text: Leave something in the bowl and walk on

effects.log: The eyes close again. The moss has not noticed you were there.

events.text: A carter is screaming under a broken axle in the road, and a small plain bonesetter has already sat down on {his} chest. {He} looks up at you. "You. Strong arms. Hold the knee, and watch what I do, because I am old and nobody in this county has ever watched."

choices.text: Hold the knee, and watch

effects.log: There is one sound, and the screaming stops. {npc} shows you the same trick on a chicken bone over supper. (Bone Setting begun.)

choices.text: Hold the knee, and leave when it is done

effects.log: It is done quickly. You do not ask how, and you are not sure you wanted to know.

events.text: A woman of the river theatre cracks a silk whip at a fly on your hat, and the fly is gone and the hat is not. The crowd laughs. {npc} takes a coin off a child's nose the same way, and gives it back. "Soft things go around," {he} says to you. "Everyone here wants to learn the crack. You watched the wrist."

choices.text: Ask about the wrist

effects.log: Three weeks with the troupe and a welt on every part of you, and one morning the rope does what you meant. (Soft Whip begun.)

choices.text: Applaud and move on

effects.log: A coin thrown by the man beside you never reaches the ground. It reaches {his} hand, by the whip.

events.text: A disgraced examiner fights a drunk outside the wine shop using a sword as if correcting an essay. Three strokes, and the drunk's sleeve says "fool" in a fine running hand. {npc} sees you staring. "You hold a brush too," {he} says. "Most people who can do both are ashamed of one of them."

choices.text: Say you are ashamed of neither

effects.log: {npc} laughs until {he} coughs, and writes you a page of strokes with a blade, on a door. It takes you a year to read it. (Brush Sword begun.)

choices.text: Buy {him} the next jar instead

effects.log: It is a good evening. By the end of it {he} has insulted everyone you know, accurately.

events.text: A blind tea-house storyteller stops in the middle of a sentence to tell the room that someone on the third roof over has taken off one shoe. Everyone laughs. Later, the storyteller finds you alone. "You did not laugh," {he} says. "You looked up. Would you like to know how it is done?"

choices.text: Yes, and sit with your eyes shut

effects.log: A season of sitting in a dark room with a stranger breathing. Then one night you know exactly who is coming up the stairs. (The Listening Art begun.)

choices.text: Ask only what the shoe was for

effects.log: "Quiet on tile," says {npc}. "They were here for the magistrate's ledger." You move to a different inn.

events.text: You buy a pear from an old woman on Monday, and the next day a young soldier stops you and asks how the pear was, in the same voice. {npc} laughs at your face. "Nobody looks at a face," {he} says. "They look at how tired you are. I have been watching you. You could do this."

choices.text: Learn the borrowed walk

effects.log: For a month you are a porter, then a nun, then nobody. Your oldest friend would pass you in the street. (Thousand Faces begun.)

choices.text: Decline, and watch your purse

effects.log: Your purse is still there. A pear has been left in it.

events.text: An old standard-bearer who lost at a river forty years ago still has the flags, in a box. {He} lays them on a table among teacups. "This is the river," {he} says. "You are a clever one. You have one hundred men, and it is raining. Tell me what you do, and I will tell you when they die."

choices.text: Move a teacup

effects.log: Your hundred men are lost six times before the tea is cold. On the seventh, {npc} looks at the table for a while without speaking. (Banner Command begun.)

choices.text: Say the battle is long over

effects.log: "It is," {npc} says, and starts to put away the flags, one at a time, in the order they fell.

events.text: At a funeral in a poor village you hear it: an old mourner, under everyone else's noise, humming a line that makes your teeth feel far away. {He} stops when {he} sees you listening. "Your ear is not for the living," {he} says, not unkindly. "Most of them would have felt nothing."

choices.text: Ask {him} to teach you the line

effects.log: It has no words. It has an order in which you stop being afraid of things. You learn the first of them that winter. (Soul Chant begun.)

choices.text: Pay your respects and leave

effects.log: You leave silver for the family. The line follows you a little way down the road and then lets you go.

events.text: A hermit on a bare ridge watches you run your method, and winces as if {he} had bitten on something. "That breath and your root are at war," {he} says. "You will win, and you will have spent your life on it. Wood feeds fire. Do you know what that means, or have you only read it?"

choices.text: Admit you have only read it

effects.log: You breathe in a circle for a hundred days on the ridge, wood to fire to earth, until your root stops arguing. (Five-Phase Breath begun.)

choices.text: Say your method has served you well

effects.log: "It has," says {npc}. "Ask it what it charged."

events.text: A village schoolmaster has the slowest boy in three counties, and has been explaining the same sum since spring. You watch {him} try a ninth way, and a tenth. On the eleventh the boy looks up. {npc} sees you see it. "Everyone can do it once," {he} says. "Would you care to learn how to do it again?"

choices.text: Stay a season, and take the bench beside {him}

effects.log: You are very bad at it. Then one afternoon somebody else's child understands something, and you have to go outside. (The Art of Teaching begun.)

choices.text: Leave something for the school

effects.log: The boy carries your silver to the master with both hands, and has counted it correctly.

events.text: On the ten thousand steps of a pilgrim mountain a tiny old porter goes past you with a stove on {his} back, then comes down, then goes past you again. "You stop to breathe," {he} says on the third pass. "That is why you have to stop. Do you want to carry something?"

choices.text: Take a stove

effects.log: You carry stoves for a month, and you learn to climb the way water goes down. (Stair Breath begun.)

choices.text: Sit down on the step, and tell {him} to go on

effects.log: You sit. The view is very good. {npc} passes twice more before you get up.

events.text: A guest who has come to kill you is drinking your tea. You both know it. You pour again, slowly, and watch the shake go out of {his} hand before it goes out of yours. When you sit to meditate on the Dao these days the first breath is already the fifth. Tonight, you wonder if {he} can tell.

choices.text: Ask {him} who sent {him}, between cups

effects.log: {npc} tells you, on the third cup, and asks for a fourth. In the morning there is one fewer enemy in the province, and nobody was hurt.

choices.text: Say nothing, and see {him} to the gate

effects.log: The story goes round the province. People have started to arrive for tea who do not drink it.

events.text: A cart horse bolts in the market with a child on the shafts. Your whip is around the bridle before you have decided anything, and then you are holding a horse. Afterwards {npc} comes to you, an animal dealer, wiping {his} hands. "You did not break its mouth," {he} says. "I have a beast nobody can touch. It wants a hand like that."

choices.text: Go and look at the beast

effects.log: It bites you, then stops. You leave with a vial of its blood, freely given, and an offer of work. From now on what you best on the road may follow you home.

choices.text: Return the child and go

effects.log: The mother cannot speak. The horse tries to follow you for a while.

events.text: A form of your own has not moved for a year, and you are copying an old poem to rest. Halfway down the page you notice that the third stroke is the form. You stop and look at your hand. {npc} is at the door with an unpaid bill, and has seen your face. "Should I come back?" {he} says.

choices.text: Ask {him} to come back

effects.log: You write until the lamp is out. Your own art comes easier now, as anything does that has already been written once.

choices.text: Pay the bill, and then go back to the page

effects.log: It does not go away. It waits, as a good sentence does.

events.text: You sit across a ferry from two sect hunters who carry your description. One reads it aloud, slowly. "Tall, carries on the left, walks like someone with a grievance." You are a fat salt merchant with a cough, and you are asking {npc} here about the price of river fish. Their eyes pass over you like water.

choices.text: Offer them some fish

effects.log: One of them buys a fish from you. It is the most frightening thing you have done this year. They go on looking for you, further away.

choices.text: Get off at the next landing

effects.log: You get off. Three years later you hear they are still on that river.

events.text: At a county muster you are asked to look at the militia, as a courtesy. You move four men and a cart. {npc}, their captain, stares at the yard for a long time and then sends for {his} old map. "A sect could be beaten from here," {he} says. "If anybody ever wished to."

choices.text: Draw {him} the map

effects.log: Your name starts to appear in places a fighter's name does not. In any war your house goes to, people will stand where you tell them.

choices.text: Tell {him} to burn the map

effects.log: {npc} burns it. You watch the smoke and then you draw it again, for yourself, from memory.

events.text: You are humming under your breath, in a sickroom, for nobody in particular, and the old one in the bed sits up and tells you {npc} is at the door. {npc} is at the door. "It is your humming," the old one says. "It goes further than you do." You feel it then: the part of you that lives past the walls.

choices.text: Keep humming, and follow it

effects.log: You sit up with it until dawn. Your soul sits a little further out in you than it did yesterday.

choices.text: Stop, and see who is at the door

effects.log: {npc} has brought soup. You are grateful, afterwards, for a door with only somebody at it.

events.text: A pupil you had given up on comes back after ten years with a blade at {his} side and a sect's jade on {his} belt. {npc} bows to you in the road, in front of everyone, and then tells you a thing you once said that you do not remember saying. {He} has built {his} whole life on it.

choices.text: Pretend you remember

effects.log: You nod slowly, and {npc} is very happy. You spend the evening frightened by the things you might have said.

choices.text: Tell {him} you do not remember

effects.log: {npc} laughs for a long time. "That is the best thing you ever taught me," {he} says. You will be asked to teach again.

events.text: A partner brings you the year's books with a pleasant smile. You read them as you would read a stance, and on the eleventh page you find the one number in the book that is standing badly. {npc} watches your finger stop. {He} has stopped smiling, and is working out how much you know.

choices.text: Say nothing, and have the number corrected

effects.log: The silver turns up next month, with a note about a clerk. Your books have not been wrong since.

choices.text: Ask {him} about it, in front of the staff

effects.log: {npc} leaves the county. Every clerk you employ now sits a little straighter.

events.text: On a floor of the Tower where you once sat for a whole season gasping, you find you have come up the stair still breathing as you do on a road. {npc}, a climber sitting against the wall with {his} sword across {his} knees, looks up at you. "Are you even tired?"

choices.text: Sit down and show {him} the breath

effects.log: You sit with {npc} for an hour. The Tower does not seem to mind. Neither of you is anyone in particular, for that hour.

choices.text: Say, "Not yet," and go on up

effects.log: You go on. Your breath is the only sound on the stair, and it does not change.

events.text: For days after the ash you keep tasting it. Then a stranger stops you on a bridge and calls you by a name you have never had, and asks if you have finally paid. {He} does not seem surprised when you do not answer. "It is a start," says {npc}, and goes on across. You have three years less, and you feel lighter.

choices.text: Go after {him}, and ask what the name was

effects.log: {npc} tells you. It means nothing. In the night you remember what it means.

choices.text: Let {him} go, and leave silver at the next shrine

effects.log: You leave silver at the next shrine, and the one after. It has become a habit you did not ask for.

events.text: You are at a roadside inn, some way from anybody who should know you, when someone in the next room tells {npc} how you died. It is told well. The teller was in the cell. There is the cold of you, and the cart. You sit and eat your noodles and listen to the part where the guard cried.

choices.text: Stay dead for a while

effects.log: It is restful. Nobody wants anything from a dead person.

choices.text: Buy the storyteller a drink

effects.log: The storyteller looks at you for a long time, and takes the drink. The story is better the next night.

events.text: The sickness of the Empty Bowl takes a whole month to pass. When you can stand, you take a lesser pill to test it, and it goes in as it did when you were young. {npc}, the apothecary, looks at your tongue and your eyes. "You will not find that a second time," {he} says. "Spend it on something."

choices.text: Ask what {he} would spend it on

effects.log: {npc} tells you. It is not what you expected, and it is not a pill.

choices.text: Buy what {he} has that is any good

effects.log: It is good, and you can feel it land.

events.text: The Root-Turning Pill has done its work, and your old method runs without the old quarrel in it. Then an elder of your root's own element meets you on the road, and stops dead. "What have you done?" says {npc}, staring at something you cannot see. "It leans. Your root leans. Who did that to you?"

choices.text: Say you did it yourself

effects.log: {npc} looks at you as if at an interesting death. {He} writes it down.

choices.text: Ask whether it can be read

effects.log: {npc} reads it, there on the road, with two fingers on your wrist. {He} does not stop frowning, and {he} does not stop reading.

events.text: Evening in the village. The neighbours have brought out the bad wine, and {npc} is telling the one about the goat for the fifth time this year. You laugh in the right place. You notice you did not have to remember to. Somewhere very far under you, something sealed turns over in its sleep and does not wake.

choices.text: Tell the one about the goat yourself, next time

effects.log: You tell it badly. It becomes your story anyway. They call it yours.

choices.text: Go home early and sit with it

effects.log: You sit. It is quiet. You are, you notice, not unhappy, and you leave that alone.

events.text: A tutor comes to your door with a slate. {He} has been teaching the young one of your house for a season and has now been corrected, on a point {he} has held for thirty years, by a child eating a pear. "I do not know what you did," says {npc}. "I would like to know what you intend to do about it."

choices.text: Send for better teachers, at any price

effects.log: They come, and leave, one by one, somewhat quieter. The child does not notice them go.

choices.text: Ask {him} to stay and be corrected

effects.log: {npc} stays, and it is the happiest {he} has been in years. The two of them argue at breakfast.

events.text: The neighbour {npc} stops you on the path and asks what you did. The old one in your house was up on the roof this morning, mending it, and shouted down at {him} about a debt from twenty years ago. "We were all so sure," {he} says. {He} does not sound entirely pleased. "Is there any more of it?"

choices.text: Send over a bowl of the plain soup

effects.log: It is only soup. {npc} is better within the week, and tells everyone.

choices.text: Say it does not work on people who ask

effects.log: {npc} laughs and nearly believes you. You go up and help with the roof.

events.text: They say you can see it now on those who have tried a gate on a Burning pill. {npc}, an old gate-guard of some forgotten sect, sees it on you across a market. {He} points to {his} own throat, where the scar goes down. "Once," {he} says. "We all think once. Did it open?"

choices.text: Say what happened

effects.log: {npc} listens to all of it. {He} tells you {his} own, and it is much worse, and {he} asks you to stop there.

choices.text: Ask who sells them

effects.log: {npc} tells you, and looks away first.
